label: conj:kashaev-density-equals-sdp-multiplicity
title: Kashaev density prefactor equals joint-tower SDP Wedderburn multiplicity ($\rho_F = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}$)
html:
(Conditional.) Under the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture applied to an atomic Hecke element T_w with Markov closure knot/link K_w, the multiplicative density prefactor \rho_F \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} in the binding-energy formula

  B_{\mathrm{pred}}(K_w)
  \;=\;
  \rho_F \cdot m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(K_w)

equals the joint-tower SDP Wedderburn multiplicity \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(K_w) of the canonical Hecke element T_w's saturating SDP solution in the H_{n}(q) Wedderburn decomposition:

  \rho_F  \;=\;  \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(K_w)

per atom-knot-mass-derivation §Algorithm step 3 (the joint-tower SDP solve that produces \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} as a non-negative integer multiplicity).

Evidence (two confirmed atoms)

The identity is exact on the SDP-confirmed hyperbolic atoms (per atom-knot-mass-derivation line 265):

Atom K_w \rho_F (legacy) \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}
{}^{3}\mathrm{H} (T) knot 8_{11} 2 2
{}^{3}\mathrm{He} link L_{6a4} 2 2

The deuterium row that once headed this table has been removed, and the removal is not bookkeeping. It read {}^{2}\mathrm{H} \mid 6_2 \mid 1 \mid 1, assigning the deuteron the census knot 6_2 with \mathrm{Vol} \approx 4.40. The canonical deuteron knot is the braid closure (trefoil / Hopf), with \mathrm{Vol} = 0; the 6_2 assignment is retired, and the deuteron binding is not a hyperbolic-volume term. Since the identity's own formula is B_{\mathrm{pred}}(K) = \rho_F \, \mathfrak{m}_e \, \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(K), at \mathrm{Vol} = 0 it returns B_{\mathrm{pred}} = 0 for every value of \rho_F — so that row could not constrain the prefactor even in principle. It was not a stale entry contributing weak support; it was contributing none.

The evidence base for the \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} pattern is therefore two points, both equal to 2, not three points reading 1, 2, 2. The 1 was the row now removed, so the variation in that pattern came entirely from it.

Read this together with an operational finding: six operational definitions of \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} were computed and none reproduces the legacy triple, and the committed values carry the methodology tag "manual-historical-volume-match" — they are hand-assigned rather than derived.

The {}^{4}\mathrm{He} case uses the magic A \cdot 8G closure rule rather than a census knot. A binding-arbiter probe against AME2020 does not confirm an integer \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(⁴\mathrm{He}): the data-pinned prefactor is \rho_F(⁴\mathrm{He}) = B_{\mathrm{AME}}/(m_e A\,8G) \approx 1.889, which sits strictly between the isospin count (2T{+}1 = 1, T{=}0) and the monotone Wedderburn count (A{-}1 = \mathrm{sc}(3A) = 3). No clean categorical integer count reproduces 1.889; rounding it to 2 has no derived origin. Consequently the identity \rho_F = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} is scoped to the census-knot / linear-chain atoms ({}^{3}\mathrm{H}, {}^{3}\mathrm{He}), where \rho_F = A{-}1 is exact and the SDP framing is canonical. At the doubly-magic point the prefactor is an empirical effective binding coefficient (\approx 1.89, Coulomb-corrected \approx 1.94), not an integer categorical multiplicity.

Categorical home

This identity is of the MacMahon-style partition-algebra type. The Wedderburn multiplicity of T_w's SDP solution is a partition-algebra count: it is the dimension of the saturating projection in the irreducible-block decomposition H_n(q) \cong \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda). The agreement with the Kashaev density factor identifies \rho_F as such a count.

The published MacMahon-type statement about the colored Jones function is the Garoufalidis--Loebl formula. With \mathrm{Ferm}(A) = \sum_{J} (-1)^{|J|} \det_q(A_J) the alternating sum of quantum minors, which reduces to \det(I - A) at q = 1 where the MacMahon Master Theorem inverts it as \sum_n \mathrm{tr}\,S^n(A), every knot diagram K has an arc-graph matrix B'_K with J_n(K,q) = q^{\delta(K,n)} / \mathrm{Ferm}(B'_K), n-evaluated [garoufalidis-loebl2005, §1, Def. 1.4 and Thm. 2]. That theorem expresses J_n as the inverse of a non-commutative fermionic partition function; it is not a statement about Wedderburn multiplicities of H_n(q), so the identification of \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} as a partition-algebra count above is made here and is not supplied by it.

Conditional structure

The conjecture is conditional on the joint-tower SDP completeness: i.e. the joint-tower SDP solver of the canonical formalism, which does not yet exist, gives a unique non-negative integer \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(K_w) for every bound-state knot K_w. Until that solver is available, the identity is verified on two census atoms and extrapolated to {}^{4}\mathrm{He} with explicit caveat. The hypothesis asserts, for each atom a with volume \mathrm{Vol}(a) > 0 and with m_e > 0, a positive integer \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(a) such that \rho_F(a) = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(a), together with the binding formula B_{\mathrm{pred}}(a) = \rho_F(a)\, m_e\, \mathrm{Vol}(a).

The quantities \rho_F, \mathrm{Vol} and m_e are given data rather than existentials, so the hypothesis is refutable: a prefactor lying strictly between two consecutive naturals — as the {}^{4}\mathrm{He} datum \rho_F \approx 1.889 does — admits no \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} at all.

The hypothesis is not established. That is the open state: establishing it would require supplying \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}, and no operational definition in the corpus yet reproduces the confirmed 1, 2, 2. The hypothesis deliberately does not identify \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} with any SDP construction — the Wedderburn saturating projection whose dimension it is meant to be is not constructed here — so what it states is the positive-integrality of the prefactor and the binding formula it feeds, and nothing more.

Notation hazard resolved

Before the present convention, three distinct quantities used the symbol \rho in QOU compute and content (per atom-knot-mass-derivation §Notation):

  • \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} — integer Wedderburn multiplicity (this conjecture)
  • \rho_K — CODATA-fit density per knot
  • \rho_F — Kashaev prefactor in the formal derivation (unnamed, compute-only)

The present convention consolidates around the canonical \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} name, removing the third unnamed \rho.

Where \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} is used

  • the atom assignment of the binding computation, which reads \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} and emits B_{\mathrm{pred}} = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} \cdot m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(K)
  • atom-knot-mass-derivation §Algorithm step 3 — supplies \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} via joint-tower SDP

What remains open

  1. {}^{4}\mathrm{He} resolved (negative). The binding-arbiter probe found \rho_F(⁴\mathrm{He}) \approx 1.889 — not an integer, and no categorical count derives the cap at 2 (see §Evidence). The open successors are sharper: (a) is \rho_F even integer-valued at doubly-magic nuclei? and (b) derive the doubly-magic prefactor directly (including Coulomb), rather than rounding 1.89 \to 2. The census-knot atoms ({}^{3}\mathrm{H}, {}^{3}\mathrm{He}) remain the exact domain of the \rho_F = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} identity; {}^{2}\mathrm{H} left that domain when its knot assignment was retired (see §Evidence).
  2. Extend joint-tower SDP to {}^{5}\mathrm{Li}, {}^{6}\mathrm{Li}, {}^{7}\mathrm{Li} — the A\in{5,6,7} gap needs \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} values; the wider atom\toknot census is deferred until the full SDP solver is available.
  3. Extend joint-tower SDP to α-cluster atoms ({}^{8}\mathrm{Be} and up) — the α-cluster rule inherits \rho_F = 2 from {}^{4}\mathrm{He}; verifying \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} = 2 across the α-cluster recursion would close the inheritance step.
